STILLROOT'S SONG   |   GM DOSSIER

Map-pin index

The village map is supplied separately by the GM. This journal adds no invented coordinates and no replacement Scene. Place Journal Notes on the actual map and select the relevant page. Map images are not bundled with this module.

If a landmark is not on the finished map, place its scene inside an existing building or use it as a dream room. Do not stop the session to redesign terrain.

Connections

The inn, bakery, tailor, chapel and square are a short walk apart. Hearthhouse borders the orchard. The orchard path leads to the crystal formation. The ruins/cellar and the well both lead to the under-village cistern. The dream reproduces these connections with distortions, but the red thread remains a usable route.

STILLROOT'S SONG   |   GM DOSSIER

Ordinary life with one wrong seam

Square: three benches, a dry rim around the well, a noticeboard advertising a harvest supper. The attendance count has been corrected downward without changing the number of meals ordered.

Chapel: polished wood, damp wool, a faint trace of incense. A bell rope disappears through the ceiling. Hoss insists there has never been a bell tower. The rope is still ordinary rope and can be followed.

Forge: good work, well-maintained tools, two heights of worn handles. Torbin has large hands; the smaller set belonged to Oren. Thomlin knows whose tools they are until someone contradicts him.

Orchard: windfall apples are gathered neatly in rows that resemble place settings. Nella's left footprint misses a triangular patch. Tracks can be measured and followed.

Graveyard: several graves have family symbols but no names. Dirt under the headstones is old; these are not fresh murders. A mourner can describe an anniversary while unable to name the person mourned.

Ruins: old fitted stone, a modern lock and a recently replaced hinge. An ordinary route has been maintained through a supposedly abandoned place.

Three lines for nameless villagers

'You're staying? Good. Travellers never seem to stay.'

'Everyone who belongs here is here.'

'I did set two cups. I always set two cups. Is that unusual?'

Give a villager a concrete task and an immediate worry unrelated to the horror. Their humanity makes the contradictions matter.
